change: Reserve an unnameable Dewy comprehension accumulator once for straight-line 0..n exclusive int64 ranges. Write plain values by a stable iteration index; managed elements or mutable loop bindings use reserved append with incremental length. General control flow retains ordinary append. Dotted assignments at the end of comprehension blocks are recognized as statements.
validation: Independent C bootstrap and full gate: 5081 checks passed in 186.49s of pytest time. Earlier focused checks passed (186 in 3.93s). Ruff and git diff --check passed.

benchmark.compile_conclusion: CPU time is essentially unchanged; wall time was noisy (including higher tour/Netpong medians), so no wall-clock improvement claim.

coverage: negative/empty signed bounds, narrow and unsigned fallback ranges
bound evaluated once before callbacks that modify it
plain records, managed arrays and dictionary entries, value independence and cleanup
early break over int64.max does not trigger eager reservation; nested/control-flow fallbacks
input array bounds failures remain checked
full native/web, editor, watch, networking and rendering corpus
limits: Optimization is currently limited to straight-line exclusive 0..n ranges with int64 bounds.
The benchmark includes result allocation/free; C and Dewy use their own allocators.
Default builds still lag C, especially on cache-resident small arrays.
No general C parity claim. Fused controls vary slightly in the larger memory workload; small controls are essentially unchanged.
Performance used previous-core build-1792318660839262234; the independent C-bootstrap build validated the same compiler sources.
